about.title: Foster City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Foster City's tidy grid of lagoons and boulevards still funnels heavy commuter traffic through a handful of key corridors, and that traffic shows up in the numbers: 107 injury collisions and 139 people hurt in the most recent year on record, with two lives lost. SR-92, Foster City Boulevard, and E Hillsdale Boulevard carry the bulk of that volume, and local data shows crashes cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., right as commuters and school traffic overlap. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the aftermath can feel disorienting — medical visits, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect injured Foster City residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the claim and explain the options, free of charge and with no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: What Matters After a Foster City Crash

items.title: Your Filing Window Is Limited
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, but claims involving a government entity — like a road defect on SR-92 — can require notice in as little as six months. Getting guidance early helps avoid losing that window.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the collision, though your share of fault reduces the total. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated by the other side.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Undercut You Later
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, but those statements can be used to minimize your claim down the road. It's worth speaking with an independent attorney before agreeing to give one.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Foster City?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity is involved — for example, a hazard on a city-maintained road — the notice deadline can be as short as six months, so it's best not to wait.

items.question: Why does the Tuesday afternoon crash pattern on SR-92 matter for my claim?
items.answer: Public collision data shows crashes in Foster City tend to cluster on Tuesdays between 3 and 5 p.m., often tied to commuter volume near SR-92 and Foster City Boulevard. This pattern can help an attorney understand traffic conditions at the time of your crash, which may be relevant to how the incident is evaluated.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: Generally, it's wise to hold off. Recorded statements are often used to find inconsistencies or minimize what's owed to you, and you're not typically required to give one to the other side's insurer. An independent attorney can advise you on how to communicate with adjusters.
